name: COVID-19
fact: The first recognized cluster was reported in Wuhan in December 2019. COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2 and mainly spreads through respiratory particles.

name: SARS
fact: The first recognized SARS cases appeared in Guangdong in November 2002. The coronavirus later spread internationally during the 2003 outbreak.

name: AIDS
fact: The first CDC report of cases later recognized as AIDS described five patients in Los Angeles. HIV was later identified as the cause of AIDS.

name: Mpox
fact: The first reported human case was a nine-month-old boy in what was then Zaire. The virus had previously been discovered in research monkeys in 1958.

name: Legionnaires' disease
fact: A major pneumonia outbreak occurred among people attending an American Legion convention. The illness was later linked to Legionella bacteria spread through contaminated water droplets.

name: H5N1 avian influenza (human infection)
fact: The first known human H5N1 infections occurred during a poultry outbreak. Eighteen people were infected and six died.

name: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome
fact: A cluster of severe respiratory illness led to recognition of the syndrome. Infection is associated with exposure to infected rodent urine, droppings, or saliva.

name: Chikungunya
fact: The virus was first identified during an outbreak in Tanzania. It is spread by mosquitoes and is especially known for causing severe joint pain.

name: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
fact: Human RSV strains were isolated from infants with respiratory illness in Baltimore after a related virus had first been found in laboratory chimpanzees.

name: Q fever
fact: The disease was first investigated among slaughterhouse workers with an unexplained fever. The Q originally stood for 'query' because the cause was unknown.

name: H7N9 avian influenza (human infection)
fact: China reported the first three known human H7N9 infections in 2013. Severe pneumonia was common, and live-bird exposure became an important concern.

name: Rotavirus infection
fact: Researchers identified rotavirus in children hospitalized with severe gastroenteritis. It later became recognized as a major cause of severe diarrhea in young children worldwide.

name: Human metapneumovirus infection
fact: Researchers identified the virus in children with respiratory illness. Later studies showed that the virus had actually been circulating in humans for decades.

name: Variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
fact: This rare fatal prion disease was first reported in the United Kingdom and was linked to eating beef from cattle infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy.

name: Enterovirus A71 infection
fact: The virus was first identified in the United States. It is an important cause of hand, foot and mouth disease and can occasionally cause serious neurologic illness.

name: Enterovirus D68 infection
fact: EV-D68 was first isolated from children with pneumonia and bronchiolitis. It usually causes respiratory illness but has also been associated with neurologic complications.

name: Toxic shock syndrome
fact: The syndrome was first described in children in Denver. It is caused by toxins produced by certain strains of Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes.

name: E. coli O157:H7 infection
fact: The pathogen was first recognized during two outbreaks linked to contaminated hamburgers. It can cause bloody diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome.

name: Helicobacter pylori infection
fact: Robin Warren and Barry Marshall cultured the bacterium from the human stomach and showed its strong connection to gastritis and peptic ulcers.

name: Parvovirus B19 infection
fact: The virus was discovered accidentally in a blood donor sample. Its name came from the sample label: number 19 in panel B.

name: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS)
fact: A novel tick-borne virus was identified after patients developed high fever and very low platelet counts. It can cause severe or fatal disease.

name: Babesiosis
fact: The first documented human case involved a patient without a spleen. Babesia parasites infect red blood cells and are usually transmitted by ticks.

name: Human monocytic ehrlichiosis
fact: The first recognized U.S. case followed a tick bite in rural Arkansas. The infection can cause fever, headache, muscle aches, and low blood-cell counts.

name: Anaplasmosis
fact: The disease was first recognized in patients from Minnesota and Wisconsin. It is transmitted by blacklegged ticks, the same ticks that can spread Lyme disease.

name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
fact: German neurologists Hans Gerhard Creutzfeldt and Alfons Maria Jakob described cases of the rare, rapidly progressive and fatal prion disease.

name: Human bocavirus infection
fact: Swedish researchers discovered this parvovirus in respiratory samples from children. It is commonly detected in young children with respiratory illness.

name: Kuru
fact: Kuru was documented among the Fore people and later shown to be a prion disease. Transmission was linked to traditional mortuary practices involving infected nervous tissue.

name: Botulism
fact: A major outbreak of 'sausage poisoning' helped define the illness. The name botulism comes from the Latin word botulus, meaning sausage.

name: Adenovirus infection
fact: Researchers first isolated adenoviruses from cultured adenoid tissue. The viruses can cause respiratory, eye, gastrointestinal, and urinary infections.

name: Melioidosis
fact: The disease was first described at Rangoon General Hospital. It is caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, a bacterium found in soil and water in tropical regions.
